clue.text: Treat the plane in order to produce glossy skin

indicators.note: putting things in order means rearranging them, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: Instructions for dressing an aeroplane's surface to give it a shiny finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order to produce' reads as a purpose clause; 'in order' is the anagram signal and 'to produce' links it to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Patent leather is hide given a hard, mirror-like varnished finish.

clue.text: Form of defence favoured to 'get around a charge

indicators.note: one word is made to go around the outside of the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a pet is a favoured one, as in teacher's pet
a rap is a criminal charge, as in 'beat the rap'

explanation.surface: A soldier's favoured tactic for wriggling out of an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' suggests an attack, fitting the military surface, but here it is the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall or bank sheltering defenders on a rampart.

clue.text: The first to go up and match religious collection

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match
pi is informal for pious, i.e. religious
a lot is a collection of items, as at an auction

explanation.surface: Someone gets up and pairs with a church's offertory.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a crossword convention for 'religious'; a Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: A test pilot flies new aircraft before anyone else, so is first into the air.

clue.text: Suffering hardship from knee dysfunction

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows, spanning both

explanation.surface: Someone is struggling because of a bad knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Needy people are poor and lack life's necessities.

clue.text: Coastal area said to be dull

indicators.note: words describing speech show that the word heard is spelt differently from the entry

parts.note: literal means prosaic and unimaginative, i.e. dull

explanation.surface: A stretch of seaside is reputedly boring.
explanation.definitionFit: A littoral is the shore region of a sea or lake.

clue.text: Principal lady is heartless in 'a roguish way

parts.note: arch means chief or principal, as in archenemy

indicators.note: losing the heart means only the outside letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A leading lady behaves cruelly and mischievously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is heartless' strips the middle AD from LADY to leave LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Archly describes behaving in a playfully knowing or mischievous manner.

clue.text: Fillet, for example, as top treat

parts.note: the head is the top of something
to dress a wound is to treat it

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a fillet of meat as the best treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fillet' looks like a cut of fish or meat; it is also a band worn round the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fillet is a narrow ribbon or band worn around the head, a kind of hair ornament.

clue.text: Law teacher's talk cut short

indicators.note: a word cut short loses its final letter

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for talking at length, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork'

explanation.surface: A law lecturer's lecture is abruptly ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rabbit (on)' is British slang for chatter; 'cut short' drops its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a scholar and teacher of Jewish religious law.

clue.text: Vehicles used to slow motion

definitions.meaning: old horse-drawn carriages, and later estate cars
devices that reduce a machine's speed

explanation.definitionFit: Brakes are both large carriages or estate-type vehicles and the devices that slow a moving vehicle.

clue.text: Show consideration towards relation

definitions.meaning: ... means reference, as in 'with ... to' = in relation to

explanation.definitionFit: Respect is a verb for esteeming someone and a noun for reference or regard to something.

clue.text: It's hot in the banking hall

indicators.note: one letter is placed inside the other word

parts.note: camber is the sloping or banking of a road surface
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: It is warm inside the bank's main hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banking' looks financial but means the tilt of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A chamber is a large room or hall, such as a council chamber.

clue.text: Attractive girl reports youth leader

parts.note: pops are loud reports, sharp bangs

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pretty girl is said to be leading a youth group.
explanation.definitionFit: Popsy is dated British slang for a pretty young woman.

clue.text: Drunken lawyer needed this to stay dry?

parts.note: oiled is slang for drunk
a silk is a Queen's or King's Counsel, a senior barrister who wears a silk gown

explanation.surface: A tipsy barrister required waterproofing.
explanation.walkthrough: A silk is a senior British barrister (KC), so called from the silk gown.
explanation.definitionFit: Oiled silk is fabric soaked in oil to make it waterproof, used for raincoats.

clue.text: Fashion little stone animal charm

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: Carve a small stone figure of a creature as a lucky charm.
explanation.definitionFit: A talisman is an object thought to bring luck or ward off harm, like an amulet.

clue.text: The way in which players have to negotiate

definitions.text: The way in which players have to negotiate

parts.words: The way in which players have to negotiate
parts.note: reads as a manner of bargaining by sportsmen, but describes the entrance actors pass through at a theatre

explanation.definitionFit: A stage door is the backstage entrance actors use to enter the theatre.

clue.text: Time off in secluded spot

definitions.meaning: a break from work, such as a school or parliamentary holiday

explanation.definitionFit: Recess means both a break from business and a hidden corner or alcove.

clue.text: One of 8 tea crates damaged

indicators.note: damaged crates are broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some boxes of tea have been knocked about.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer to 8 down, a word for these vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car, an old-fashioned word for which is a shooting brake, is a type of vehicle like those at 8.

clue.text: Peacekeepers misrepresent figurehead's lack of faith

parts.note: UN stands for United Nations, whose troops keep the peace
to belie is to give a false impression of
read as figure's head, the first letter of figure

explanation.surface: UN troops distort a leader's absence of religion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figurehead' splits as 'figure head', the initial F of figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbelief is the absence of religious belief, doubt or scepticism.

clue.text: Net return of associate cut back

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the word is read in reverse
cutting the back off removes the final letter

parts.note: a partner is an associate in business

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a tennis net and a partner's shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut back' drops the last R of PARTNER, giving PARTNE, which 'return of' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: To net something is to catch it in a snare, to trap.

clue.text: No leading players getting bonuses

definitions.meaning: film or stage ... are minor actors with no starring part

explanation.definitionFit: Extras are both background actors and added perks.

clue.text: One fixed payment in advance includes liqueur

indicators.note: one word contains the other pieces within it

parts.note: an ante is a stake put in before a poker hand
I is the Roman numeral for one
set means fixed or firm

explanation.surface: A flat-rate advance payment covers a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed payment' looks like one phrase; 'fixed' is a separate piece and 'payment in advance' another.
explanation.definitionFit: Anisette is a sweet aniseed-flavoured liqueur.

clue.text: For example, love to dance as morale-booster

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
love is zero in tennis, O
to trip is to dance lightly, as in trip the light fantastic

explanation.surface: Love-making as a way of cheering oneself up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an act done mainly to boost one's self-esteem.

clue.text: Warning shot called for surrender

parts.note: fore is the warning a golfer shouts
a go is a shot, an attempt

explanation.surface: A warning shot calls on someone to give up.
explanation.walkthrough: FOREGO is a variant spelling of forgo, to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To forgo is to do without or give up, relinquish.

clue.text: Golf match attracting the proverbial crowd -number unspecified

parts.note: from the proverb 'two's company, three's a crowd'
some indicates an unspecified quantity

explanation.surface: A golf game drawing a big gallery of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb is 'two's company, three's a crowd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A threesome is a golf game for three players, one playing against two.

clue.text: Beef, perhaps, in pan

definitions.meaning: a ... joint, beef being one example
to pan is to criticise harshly

explanation.definitionFit: A roast is a joint of meat such as beef, and to roast is to criticise severely.

clue.text: Fortune to put together in game of chance

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or fortune

explanation.surface: Wealth gathered in a gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery or a bingo-type game decided by luck.

clue.text: Burdens women no longer single

indicators.note: single is I, one, which is removed from the word

parts.note: ladies are women

explanation.surface: Married women carry heavy loads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'single' means I, the numeral one; 'no longer single' takes it out of LADIES.
explanation.definitionFit: To lade is to load, so lades means loads or burdens.

clue.text: Solitary sailor collected seafood

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman
alone means solitary

explanation.surface: A lone sailor gathers shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: AB stands for able seaman in crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Abalone is an edible shellfish, a sea snail prized as food.

clue.text: In crude form, a persuader

indicators.note: putting the word into a new form rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: Someone coaxing others in a rough way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' stays as it is; 'form' rearranges CRUDE to give DUCER.
explanation.definitionFit: An inducer is one who brings about or prompts, someone who persuades.

clue.text: Quickly removed football kit and dressed down

definitions.meaning: literally pulled off one's strip, the British word for a team's kit
to tear someone off a strip is British slang for reprimanding them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both pulling off a team kit and rebuking someone angrily.
